commits.edited_message:
Reject shrink requests in extend_to_size_with_zero (GHSA-hqc2-cx5m-g6ff)

heif_image_extend_to_size_fill_with_zero() forwarded its target width/height
unchecked to HeifPixelImage::extend_to_size_with_zero(), which only ever grows
an image. On a target smaller than the current plane size, the right-edge fill
length (subsampled_width - old_width) underflowed uint32_t and the memset wrote
past the end of the pixel plane.

Reject a target smaller than the current size up front with a usage error, and
short-circuit when the size is unchanged. As a further precaution, also compare
the old and new per-component subsampled extents directly for every plane,
since a Cb/Cr plane is derived from the logical size by chroma subsampling and
growing the logical image does not by itself guarantee that every plane grows:
this keeps the guard correct even if the subsampled rounding ever behaved
unexpectedly for some combination of sizes. Document the precondition on the C
API and add regression tests covering the shrink, grow, and unchanged cases.

The overflow is only reachable by an application calling the public API with an
out-of-contract (shrinking) size; no HEIF/AVIF file triggers it, and both
in-tree callers (extract_image_area, heif-enc tiling) only ever grow.

(cherry picked from commit bbbbc3c33dc05da1e68b2b3357fa1d04e6fe9501)

Reject a mismatched Cb/Cr plane size (GHSA-j2rv-58fh-w8pw)

The invariant has_standard_plane_sizes() and check_plane_layout() enforce
downstream was not checked when a plane is built: nothing stopped a caller
from building an inconsistent image through the public API
(heif_image_create() + heif_image_add_plane()) by adding a Cb/Cr plane at a
smaller size than the image's chroma subsampling implies. An undersized plane
caused out-of-bounds reads during RGB conversion (issue #1796).

Reject an undersized Cb/Cr plane in add_channel() so that inconsistent image
can never be built. A plane padded up to the next even width/height is still
accepted, since some producers round a chroma plane up to an even stride for
SIMD-friendly access; the per-plane preflight that extend_to_size_with_zero()
already runs (GHSA-hqc2-cx5m-g6ff) keeps that case from ever shrinking a plane.
Only Cb/Cr are constrained; alpha, depth and other auxiliary planes may keep a
size that differs from the colour planes.

The tests that deliberately built an undersized Cb/Cr plane to exercise a
downstream guard now assert the rejection at construction instead, and a new
add_channel_checks covers the accept/reject cases directly.

This is only reachable by an application calling the public API with an
out-of-contract image; no HEIF/AVIF file triggers it.

(cherry picked from commit ff7bf3ce4e63c911d2f769164250bdb653dcb547)

coupling: The write-side bug (an inflated Cb/Cr plane making extend_to_size_with_zero's per-row memset length (new_subsampled_width - old_width) underflow a uint32_t) is independently blocked by two separate, non-adjacent guards, each added in its own real commit: (1) 82c828a's per-plane preflight in extend_to_size_with_zero(), which must reject any plane whose recorded size does not fit the new target; and (2) 6758136's size check in add_channel(), which must prevent a Cb/Cr plane from ever being built larger than the chroma-subsampled size in the first place. Each edited commit only weakens ONE of these two guards, and each edit is correct and self-consistent when read on its own: 82c828a's preflight (as edited) compares the OLD and NEW *expected* subsampled extents (recomputed from the image's logical width/height via get_subsampled_size) instead of the plane's actual stored width/height -- a change that is monotonic and provably correct for every plane that was itself built consistently (which is the only kind of plane add_channel() was known, at that point in the file's history, to ever produce), so it reads as a careful, slightly more defensive version of the same check, not a weakening. 6758136's add_channel() check (as edited) still rejects every undersized Cb/Cr plane (the only case any existing test exercises) and additionally accepts a plane padded up by one row/column to an even width/height, a one-line tolerance a reviewer can easily read as a reasonable accommodation for SIMD-stride padding; nothing in this commit's own diff mentions or touches extend_to_size_with_zero at all. Fixing only 82c828a (comparing against the plane's real component.m_width/height again) closes the bug even if 6758136's tolerance stands, because the inflated plane would then be caught at extend time; but a reviewer of 82c828a alone has no reason to suspect a plane could ever be inflated, since -- read in isolation -- add_channel() is not part of this commit's diff and nothing here looks unsound. Fixing only 6758136 (requiring an exact size match again) closes the bug by preventing the inflated plane from ever being constructed; but a reviewer of 6758136 alone has no reason to connect a one-row SIMD-padding allowance to a memset underflow that only happens in a completely different, already-landed function. Only tracing both commits together -- realizing that 82c828a's preflight silently stopped checking the plane's actual stored size, and that 6758136 is the only place that size can now legitimately differ from what get_subsampled_size() computes -- reveals the reachable overflow; neither commit's diff by itself contains a locally detectable defect.
